properties.statement:
A PROJECT CAN RUN REFLOW2 WITH NO KIT INSTALLED, AND NOTHING IN THE SURFACE SAYS SO. A STALE KIT IS DETECTED; AN ABSENT ONE IS SILENT. Reported by dev_storyflow's api-boss sidekick (`551d9718`), 2026-08-15, measured on their own project.

WHAT THEY MEASURED: dev_storyflow has been designed in reflow2 since 2026-07-21 — MCP tools, served skills, a live shared server on 0.31.0, 1,590 nodes, and a committed export tracked in git. It does NOT have `.reflow2/kit-version.json`, `tools/reflow2_check.py` or `tools/loop_nudge.py`. A find across both their repos returned zero hits.

⇒ THE CONSUMER CI COHERENCE GATE HAS NEVER EXISTED IN THE PROJECT IT WAS BUILT FOR, and its one prerequisite — a committed export — has been satisfied the whole time. `getting-started/SETUP.md` says '`tools/reflow2_check.py` (in the kit)', which is true OF THE KIT and false of this installation.

⭐ WHY THE ONE SIGNAL PRESENT DID NOT HELP, and this is the sharp part. `loop_status` does emit `"nudge": "absent"` with an advisory — but that advisory is about the SESSION-END NUDGE. A fleet with its own harness Stop hook (this one has) reads it, correctly concludes 'covered, not my problem', and moves on. NOTHING ANYWHERE SAYS THE CI GATE IS ALSO MISSING. Two absences, one report, and the report names the wrong one.

CORROBORATED FROM THIS SESSION'S OWN SURFACE: every `loop_status` call here returned `"nudge": "installed"` and NO kit field of any kind. Installation state is not something the tool can be asked about.

⭐⭐ THE ARGUMENT THEY OFFER RATHER THAN THE REQUEST, and it is the better half: `check_kit_manifest.py` already answers 'does an installed kit agree with its source?' — a question that PRESUPPOSES A KIT. The unasked question is 'is there one?', and it is the one that fails toward calm. A STALE KIT IS DETECTED, AN ABSENT KIT IS SILENT. Same family as the directory-artifact crash: a check honest about the case it was built for and mute about the case one step outside it.

PAIRS WITH `fact:defect-a-stale-kit-receipt-silently-decides-whether-the-loop-nudge-is-owed`, from Alex's report the same day, and TOGETHER THEY SAY SOMETHING NEITHER SAYS ALONE: `.reflow2/kit-version.json` is READ (the nudge branches on its `harnesses` key) and NEVER REPORTED. One file, consulted for a narrow harness decision, carrying the only evidence of whether the consumer half of the product is installed at all — and no tool surfaces it. Alex's case was a stamp twenty versions stale; theirs is no stamp at all; both are invisible for the same reason.

THEIR ASK, cheapest first: have `loop_status` or `graph_report` report kit installation state as ITS OWN FIELD, distinct from nudge state — `kit: absent | stale | v0.31.0`. And their framing of the tone is right: 'a project running reflow2 without the kit is not a broken project and should not be scolded, but it is STRUCTURALLY UNABLE TO GATE ON DRIFT.'

BOUND THEY STATE THEMSELVES: they did not test whether running `reflow2_init.py` on that repo now is safe — it writes into `.claude/`, which their fleet hand-built. Nothing here claims the install is a one-command fix, only that its ABSENCE is currently unreportable.

NOT ESTABLISHED: how many other consumer projects are in this state. dev_storyflow is one of three known designs and the only one measured.
